newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish chemical trader Ciech rights issue fails.
newsitem.headline: Polish chemical trader Ciech rights issue fails.

text.p: The capital raise of 19.8 million shares to 39.6 million shares in Poland's largest chemical trader, state-owned Ciech SA, will not be carried out, the company said in a statement on Friday.
The issue would have diluted the state treasury's holding in Ciech to below 50 percent from the current 53 percent.
"The Series C rights issue passed by...the extraordinary shareholders meeting of Ciech on April, 2, 1996, failed," the statement said, giving no details.
Ciech officials were unavailable for comment on Friday.
The statement said that money from the failed issue would be returned in two weeks.
Ciech currently has a share capital of 98,981,500 zlotys, 53 percent of which are held by the state treasury and the rest by numerous chemical firms, most in the state sector.

The Foreign Trade Ministry, which represents the treasury as Ciech's owner, had planned to direct part of the issue to the newly formed Chemia Polska holding, which was to invest in state-owned chemical firms and consolidate the sector.
The ministry had picked a consortium of NM Rothschild and Sons Ltd, the Polish state, Pekao SA bank and a consulting firm Access, as its adviser in the privatisation of the company.
Ciech President Zdzislaw Matkiewicz said in September that the issue would strengthen Ciech with capital before its planned listing on the Warsaw bourse in late March or early April next year.
Ciech, which employees 750, expects a 51 million zloty net profit this year against 50 million zlotys in 1995 and 48 million in 1994.
The firm, which ranks among Poland's largest companies, expects sales to rise 15.3 percent this year against $960 million in 1995 and $1.3 billion in 1994.
